title: Felkin–Anh addition of a Grignard reagent
subtitle: A stereocentre next to C=O decides which face the nucleophile attacks

reactants.caption: methylmagnesium bromide + 2-phenylpropanal (one enantiomer)
reactants.learnerPrompt: The Grignard reagent adds to an aldehyde next to a stereocentre. Draw the addition.
hintTiers: The C–Mg bond is polarised towards carbon: the methyl group acts as a carbanion. Which atom of the aldehyde is electron-poor?
The C–Mg bonding pair forms a new C–C bond to the carbonyl carbon, and the C=O π pair moves onto oxygen. Two arrows.
C–Mg bond → new C–C bond from the methyl carbon to the carbonyl carbon; C=O π bond → lone pair on oxygen.

misconceptions.feedbackMessage: The carbonyl oxygen is electron-rich. The methyl group attacks the electron-poor carbonyl carbon.
The stereocentre next to the carbonyl has no leaving group and is not electrophilic. It steers the attack, but the methyl group bonds to the carbonyl carbon.
Carbon is more electronegative than magnesium: the C–Mg bonding pair goes with carbon.

partialProgressMessages.feedbackMessage: Right: the methyl carbon attacks the carbonyl carbon. That carbon now has five bonds: move the C=O π pair.

alkoxide.caption: magnesium alkoxide: two stereocentres now, one diastereomer favoured

alkoxide-and-acid.caption: magnesium alkoxide + H₃O⁺ (work-up)
hintTiers: The alkoxide oxygen is a strong base. Which species is the acid?
The oxygen lone pair takes a proton from H₃O⁺, and that O–H bonding pair stays on water's oxygen. Two arrows.
Alkoxide oxygen lone pair → new O–H bond to a proton of H₃O⁺; that O–H bond → lone pair on water's oxygen.

misconceptions.feedbackMessage: In the flask the alkoxide is bound to magnesium; the acid now frees the alcohol. Protonate the oxygen.

partialProgressMessages.feedbackMessage: Good: the alkoxide takes a proton from H₃O⁺. Where does the O–H bonding pair go?

steps.explanationAfterStep: The arrows are those of any Grignard addition; the selectivity is in the approach. In the reacting conformation the largest group on the stereocentre (phenyl) lies perpendicular to the C=O, where its σ* orbital lowers the energy of the π* the nucleophile fills, and anti to the incoming methyl. The methyl then approaches at the Bürgi–Dunitz angle (about 107° to the C=O) past the smallest group, hydrogen, not past the methyl group. That gives one diastereomer of the alkoxide in excess. The app does not check stereochemistry yet: the drawing shows only which atoms are bonded.

steps.caption: Dilute aqueous acid is added once the addition is over (work-up).

steps.explanationAfterStep: The alkoxide becomes the alcohol. Protonation does not touch either stereocentre, so the ratio set in the addition step is the ratio of the alcohols.

mechanismSummary: Methylmagnesium bromide adds to 2-phenylpropanal like any Grignard reagent: the C–Mg pair forms the new C–C bond and the C=O π pair moves onto oxygen; acid work-up gives 3-phenylbutan-2-ol. Because the aldehyde already has a stereocentre, the two faces of the C=O are different, and two diastereomers can form. The Felkin–Anh model predicts the major one: draw the conformation with the large group (phenyl) perpendicular to the C=O, and let the nucleophile come in anti to it, at the Bürgi–Dunitz angle, past the small group (H) rather than the medium one (CH₃). Cram's original experiment gave about 2 : 1 with methyl Grignard reagents. The app does not check stereochemistry yet: the drawing shows only which atoms are bonded.
references: Clayden, Greeves and Warren, Organic Chemistry, 2nd edition (Oxford University Press), chapter 33 (Diastereoselectivity)
